la:verb:pervolo.html:
per-vŏlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n.
Lit.
To fly through or about a place: aedes,: aërium iter,: rumor agitatis pervolat alis,: Flaminiam,.—
To fly to a place: Pegasus in nitentem pervolaturus aetheram, Poët. ap. : animus velocius in hanc sedem pervolabit, .—
Transf., of swift motion in gen., to fly or dart through, to pass quickly over or through: perque volare mare ac terras (of the sun's beams),: sex et quinquaginta milia passuum cisiis pervolavit,: totam urbem,; cf.: axe citato Flaminiam,.

la:verb:pervideo.gloss: to look over or on, overlook, survey, view
senses: to look over or on, overlook, survey, view
la:verb:pervideo.html:
pervĭdĕo, vīdi, vīsum, 2, v. a.,
to look over, look on, overlook, survey.
Lit.: sol pervidet omnia,.—
Transf., to look at or upon, to view: cunctaque mens oculis pervidet illa suis,: cum tua pervideas oculis mala lippus inunctis,.—
Trop.
To consider, examine: pervideamus, utrum, etc.,: videbo te et pervidebo, (B. and K. promonebo).—
To perceive, discern, (for ; v. 2. pervolo): meritorum meorum fieri accessionem pervidere te spero,: infirmitatem animorum,; .—Hence, * per-vĭdens, entis, P. a., sagacious, intelligent: pervidentissimus princeps, dub. (al. providentissimus).

la:verb:pervulgo.html:
pervulgo or -volgo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to communicate to the people, to make publicly known, to publish, spread abroad (class.; cf. publico).
Lit.
In gen., : de re illustri et facile etiam in vulgus pervulgatā,: in re tam clarā, tam testatā, tam abs te ipso pervulgatā,: illas tabulas pervulgari atque edi populo Romano imperavi,: praemia virtutis in mediocribus hominibus pervulgari,; .—
In partic., to make one's self common, to prostitute one's self: mulier, quae se omnibus pervulgaret,.—
Transf., to visit often, to frequent, haunt a place (poet.): litus pervolgans feror, Pac. ap. Müll. (Trag. Rel. p. 108 Rib.): solis pervolgant fulgura caelum,: quae pervolgant nemora avia pervolitantes,; . —Hence, pervulgātus (pervolg-), a, um, P. a.
Very usual, very common, : at hoc pervolgatum est nimis,: consolatio pervulgata,: notius pervulgatiusque,: pervulgatissima verborum dignitas,.—
Well known: maledicta pervulgata in omnes,: humanitas,.—Adv.: pervulgātē, after the manner of the people, as the vulgar do: pervulgate magis quam inscite locutus es,; .

la:verb:pervenio.html:
per-vĕnĭo, vēni, ventum, 4 (old
fut. pervenibunt, Pompon. ap. ; pres. subj. pervenat, ; inf. pres. pass. pervenirier, ), v. n., to come to, arrive at, reach a place.
Lit.: quotumo die Sicuone huc pervenisti,: Germani in fines Eburonum pervenerunt,: ad portam,: in summum montis,: in portum,.—
Transf., of things, to reach, become known to, come to, fall to, etc.: si ad erum haec res pervenerit,: si lupinum ad siliquas non pervenit,does not come to pods, does not form pods,: duodecim secures in praedonum potestatem pervenerunt,: ut omnis hereditas ad filiam perveniret,: serrula ad Stratonem pervenit,: annona ad denarios L in singulos modios pervenerat,had risen to,: pervenit res ad istius aures,; for which poet. with simple acc.: verba aures non pervenientia nostras,.—Impers. pass.: postquam est in thalami tecta Perventum,; .—
Trop., to come to, arrive at; to reach, attain to any thing: sine me pervenire, quo

volo (in my story), : calamitas colonum ad fructus pervenire non patitur,: in maximam invidiam,: in senatum, to get into the Senate, i. e. to become a senator, : ad primos comoedos,to become a first-rate comedian,: si in tua scripta pervenero,to be mentioned in your writings,: ad id, quod cupiebat, (dub.; al. venire): ad magnam partem laudis,: deditio, ex quā ad Jugurtham scelerum impunitas, in rem publicam damna atque dedecora pervenerint,: in odium alicujus,: in amicitiam alicujus,: ex tot procellis civilibus ad incolumitatem,: ad desperationem,: in magnum timorem. ne, etc.,: ad septuagesimum regni annum pervenit,; .—Pass. impers.: pervenirier Eo quo nos volumus,attain our object,: quin erat dicturus, ad quem propter diei brevitatem perventum non est,his turn was not reached,: ad manus pervenitur,.

la:verb:perveho.gloss: to carry, bear or convey through
senses: to carry, bear or convey through
la:verb:perveho.html:
per-vĕho, xi, ctum, 3, v. a.,
to bear, carry, or convey through.
Lit.: commeatus, Liv 44, 6, 6.—Mid.: pervehi, to pass through, traverse: Oceanum pervehitur,: volucri litora classe,.—
Transf., to carry, bring, convey to a place: virgines Caere pervexit,: corpus...Romam usque pervexit,: sandaracha et ochra inde pervehuntur ad nos,: volo molliter me pervehat (sc. equus),; cf. .—Mid.: pervehi, to ride, drive, sail, etc., to come or go to a place: dictator ubi currum insidit, pervehitur usque ad oppidum, Poët. (not Enn.) ap. Müll.: in portum,; : pervectus Chalcidem,: pervectus in Africam,: Gades usque pervectus,.—Trop., to reach, attain: ad exitus optatos,.—Poet., of pedestrians, to go, come, proceed, etc.: cito passu pervecta ad litora,.

la:verb:perverto.html:
per-verto (pervorto), ti, sum, 3, v. a.,
to turn around or about, to overturn, overthrow, throw down (class.).
Lit.: pinus proceras pervortunt, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 196 Vahl.): (coqui) aulas pervortunt,: turrim ballistā,: tum visam beluam immanem, quàcunque incederet, arbusta, virgulta, tecta pervertere,: perversae rupes,broken, craggy rocks,.—
Esp., in wrestling or boxing, to throw down, knock down; hence: si rex opstabit ob viam, regem ipsum prius pervortito,.—
Trop.
To overthrow, subvert; to destroy, ruin, undo, corrupt: cito homo pervorti potest,: labefactare atque pervertere amicitiam aut justitiam,: quidam, propositis malorum et bonorum finibus, omne officium perverterunt,: omnia jura divina atque humana,: ipse (Quinctius) postquam Junium pervertit, totam causam reliquit,: hostium vim se perversurum putavit, pervertit autem suam,; : aliquem amicitiā alicujus,: aliquem,: aliquos et ambitio pervertet,.—
To put down, confute, silence one (in allusion to the meaning I. B. supra): nemo umquam me tenuissimā suspicione perstrinxit, quem non perverterim ac perfregerim,: numquam ille me opprimet consilio, numquam ullo artificio pervertet,.—Hence, perver-sus (pervorsus), a, um, P. a., turned the wrong way, askew, awry (cf. praeposterus).
Lit.: rectus perversusque partus, Varr. ap. : perversas induit comas,gets her false hair on awry,: pondere capitum perversa ova,: perversa vestis, i. e. pulla, Sen. Ira, 1, 16, 5: Roscius erat perversissimis oculis, quales sunt strabonum,dreadfully squint-eyed,.—
Trop., perverse, not right, wrong, evil, bad: dies pervorsus atque advorsus,: nihil pravum et perversum,: quid magis inquinatum, deformatum, perversum, conturbatum dici potest,: homo praeposterus atque perversus,: sapientia,: mos,: bellum Contra fata deūm perverso numine poscunt,: perversa grammaticorum subtilitas,: ambitio,: generatio perversa,wicked, et saep. —As subst.: perversum, i, n., a wrong, evil: in perversum sollers,.—Hence, adv.: perversē (pervor-sē), awry, the wrong way.
Lit.: sella curulis in senatu perverse collocata,.—
Trop., perversely, wrongly, badly, ill: dicere, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 229 Vahl.); so, dicere,: erras pervorse, pater,: interpretari,: si quid fleri pervorse videt,: vides,: si quid perverse tetreque factum est, Cato ap. : uti deorum beneficio,: imitari,: quiescite agere perverse,.—Comp.: perversius,.—Sup.: perversissime suspicari,.

la:noun:perversitas.html:
perversĭtas, ātis, f.
perversus
,
frowardness, untowardness, perversity: quae est autem in hominibus tanta perversitas, ut, etc.,: opinionum,: magna perversitas,: alicujus,: molestissima diligentiae perversitas,: morum,: incredibilis hominum,.

la:adj:pervius.gloss: having a passage through; passable, penetrable, traversable
senses: having a passage through; passable, penetrable, traversable
la:adj:pervius.html:
pervĭus, a, um, adj.
per-via
,
that has a passage through; hence,
Lit., that may be passed through or crossed, affording a passage through, passable, pervious (class.): aedes,: transitiones,thoroughfares, passages,: hostes saltus pervios ceperant,: usus Tectorum inter se,: Phoebo non pervia taxus,i. e. impervious to the sun's rays,: pervius hastis,: rima pervia flatibus,: non ulli pervia vento,: equo loca pervia,: Baianae pervia cymbae stagna,: unde maxime pervius amnis,is most fordable,: Phasis pontibus CXX. pervius,: sacraria Fauni pervia,i. e. accessible to all, not set apart by consecration,.—Hence, subst.: pervĭum, ii, n., a thoroughfare, passage: ne pervium illa Germanis exercitibus esset,.—
Transf.
Act., that makes a passage through, penetrating: ensis,.—
Pass., perforated, pierced: anulus, Fab. Pict. ap. .—
Trop.: cor meum mihi nunc pervium est, my heart is now open, i. e. light or easy, (760 Ritschl): nihil ambitioni pervium,accessible,.

la:verb:pervolito.html:
pervŏlĭto, āre,
v. freq. n. [pervolo], to fly through or around, to flit about (poet.): per dissepta domorum,; : omnia loca,: tecta,.—Transf.: iter,to traverse repeatedly,.

la:verb:pervestigo.html:
per-vestīgo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to trace out, search out.
Lit., of hounds; hence of spies: canes venaticos diceres, ita omnia odorabantur et pervestigabant, ut, etc.,.—
Trop., to seek out, examine, investigate: operam ut sumam ad pervestigandum, ubi sit illaec,; cf. ; : quae a me pervestigata et cognita sunt,: Locris sacrilegium pervestigatum a Q. Minucio erat,.

la:noun:pervicacia.html:
pervĭcācĭa, ae, f.
pervicax
,
firmness, inflexibility; in a bad sense, stubbornness, obstinacy (syn.: pertinacia, perseverantia): avaritia, ambitio, mulierositas, pervicacia,: haec pervicacia tua et superbia coëgit me loqui,: Aegyptia, Treb. Poll. .—
Transf., in a milder signif., firmness, steadiness, steadfastness: tu pertinaciam esse, hanc praedicas, ego pervicaciam aio, Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 4 Rib.; v. the entire passage under pervicax): quantā pervicaciā in hostem, tantā beneficentiā adversus supplices utendum,.— Of things: castanea pedamentis omnibus praefertur perdurandi pervicaciā,.

la:adj:pervicax.html:
pervĭcax, ācis, adj.
per and root vicof vinco
,
firm, determined; esp. in a bad sense, stubborn, obstinate, headstrong, wilful (not in Cic. or Cæs.): tu pertinaciam esse, Antiloche, hanc praedicas: Ego pervicaciam aio et eā me uti volo ... Nam pervicacem dici me esse et vincere Perfacile patior: pertinacem nil moror? Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 8 Rib.); cf.: adversus peritos pervicax,; : musa,: accusatio,; : pervicacissimi Latinorum,: pervicacioris irae fuit,: homines pervicaci audaciā, pertinaci spe,—
Of things, steady, unmoved: contra flatus pervicax libra,.—
Transf., in a good sense, steadfast, firm: recti pervicax, constans adversus metus,.—Hence, adv.: pervĭ-cācĭter, stoutly, stiffly, stubbornly, obstinately: pervicaciter perstare,. —Comp.: pervicacius causam belli quaerere,; ; fin.

la:verb:pervinco.html:
pervinco, vīci, victum, 3, v. n. and a.
Lit.
Neutr., to conquer completely, gain a complete victory: pervicit Bardanes,.—
Act., to conquer or defeat completely, gain a complete victory over: ne nos subdolā perfidiā pervincamur,: pervince, Theseu, quidquid alto in pectore Remanet pavoris,: dominae pervincere mores,.—
Transf.
To carry a point, maintain one's opinion: restitit ac pervicit .—
To surpass, outdo, exceed: sonum,.—
To induce or prevail upon with great effort, to effect with much labor, to bring about, achieve, etc.: multis rationibus pervicerat Rhodios, ut, etc.,: at illam non verbera, non ignes pervicere, quin, etc.,: pervicerunt quidem remis, ut tenerent terram,they brought it about,: neque pervincere potuit, ut referrent consules,: hoc est tibi pervincendum,; .—
To outbid in buying: si amas, eme: facito ut pretio pervincas tuo,.—
To prove, demonstrate: aliquid dictis,.
la:verb:pervinco.inflection: vīci, victum, 3, v. n. and a.

la:adj:pervetus.html:
per-vĕtus, ĕris, adj.,
very old: signum ligneum,: oppidum,, § 72: amicitia,: epistula sed sero allata,: vinum non pervetus,.

la:verb:pervigilo.gloss: to remain awake all night; keep watch all night; keep a religious vigil
senses: to remain awake all night; keep watch all night; keep a religious vigil
la:verb:pervigilo.html:
pervĭgĭlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n.,
to remain awake or watch all night; to remain awake during, to watch through any period: continuas has tris noctis pervigilavi pessume,; : vigilare leve est, pervigilare grave, and 10: noctem,: in armis,: ad luminis ignes,: nox pervigilata in mero, watched through, i. e. spent without sleep, : sollicitas trivio pervigilare moras,: Veneri,to keep a vigil all night in honor of Venus,.—
Transf., to keep watch, to watch: et tecum longos pervigilare dies,; cf.: ipsi pervigilant, quasi rationem pro animabus vestris reddituri,.

la:verb:pervagor.gloss: to wander through; to rove about
senses: to wander through; to rove about
la:verb:pervagor.html:
per-văgor, ātus, 1,
v. dep. n. and a., to wander or range through, to rove about, overrun (class.).
Lit.: hic praedonum naviculae pervagatae sunt,: iis imperat, ut omnibus in locis pervagentur,: natio pervagata bello prope orbem terrarum,; .—
Trop.
To spread out, extend: quod in exteris nationibus usque ad ultimas terras pervagatum est,: ardores in agris pervagantes,.—
To spread through, pervade: timores omnium mentes pervagantur,: dolor omnia membra pervagabatur,; .—
To be widely spread, to become common: ne is honos nimium pervagetur,.—Hence, pervăgātus, a, um, P. a.
Spread out, wide-spread, well known: longe et late pervagata anteponantur angustis,: pervagatissimus versus,: declamatio,: sermo,; cf. : gloria,.—
Common, general: pervagatior pars,of a more general nature,.

la:noun:pervigilatio.html:
pervĭgĭlātĭo, ōnis, f.
pervigil
,
a devotional watching, a vigil: nocturnae pervigilationes,.

la:verb:pervado.gloss: to pass or spread through; to pervade
senses: to pass or spread through; to pervade
la:verb:pervado.html:
per-vādo, si, sum, 3, v. a. and n.,
to go or come through, to pass or press through, to spread through (class.; syn. penetro).
Lit., constr. with acc. alone, or with per, ad, or in, and absol.: pervade polum, Att. ap. Müll. (Trag. Rel. p. 190 Rib.): incendium per agros pervasit,: per omnis partis provinciae te tamquam aliquam calamitosam pestem tempestatemque pervasisse,, § 96: ne cum in Siciliā quidem fuit ... pars ejus belli in Italiam ulla pervasit,, § 6: per aequa et iniqua loca pervadunt,: pervadere usque ad vallum,; : pars magna equitum ad terga pugnantium pervasit,: Thessaliam cum exercitu pervadit, id, 42, 13, 8: venenum ita cunctos ejus artus pervasit, ut, etc.,: impetu equi pervasit,.—In pass.: pervasā urbe,: pervasis regionibus,; .—
Transf., to go, come, arrive anywhere: ut quaedam calamitas pervadere videretur,: in nares,: ad castra,.—
Trop.
To spread through, penetrate, pervade: opinio, quae per animos gentium barbararum pervaserat,: quo non illius diei fama pervaserit,: quas oras quasi morbus quidam illius furoris pervaserat,.—With acc.: cum fama ea urbem atque forum pervasisset,: murmur totam contionem pervasit,; : pervasit jam multos ista persuasio, ut, etc.,: capesse, per deos, rem publicam, et omnia aspera pervade,to break through, overcome,: pallor ora,: magnam Asiae partem cis Euphraten tanti mali fama pervaserat,; cf.: ut quisque proximus ab oppresso sit, per omnis velut continens incendium pervasurum,: victoriae Romanae fama cum pervasisset in Asiam,: terror in totam penitus aciem pervasit,: ex contagione, velut tabes, in Perrhaebiam quoque id pervaserat malum (i. e. seditiones),. —
To arrive at, reach a place: fines,: locus, quo non nostrorum hominum libido pervaserit,.

la:verb:pervoluto.html:
pervŏlūto, āre, v. freq. a.
pervolvo
,
to roll over and over; hence, in partic., to turn over books, to look through, read: libros,: scriptores,.

la:verb:pervolvo.html:
per-volvo, volvi, vŏlūtum, 3, v. a.,
to roll or tumble about (syn. voluto).
Lit.: aliquem in luto,.—Mid., to roll one's self, to roll: in suo pervoluta sanguine,weltering,.—
Transf., to turn over a book, to read: Smyrnam incana diu saecula pervoluent,.—
Trop., to be very busy or much engaged in any thing: ut in iis locis pervolvatur animus,.
